title: Observability dashboard audit and metric prioritization notes
body:
Purpose:
- Run a lightweight, repeatable audit of existing observability dashboards and metric definitions for inference services (hosted API, dedicated, private).
- Produce a prioritized remediation backlog that reduces alert noise, closes instrumentation gaps, and surfaces cost/perf tradeoffs for product owners.

Scope:
- Dashboard surfaces: per-model route dashboards, global inference-ops landing, cost-by-tenant, rollout/canary dashboards.
- Metrics covered: latency, error, throughput, queueing, batch efficiency, KV cache hit rate, fallback/variant-rates, GPU utilization, cost-per-token.
- Traces: sampling and correlation guidance for high-cardinality routes and cross-service flows (control plane -> serving runtime -> model host).

Context / Why now:
- Several teams reported inconsistent p99 latencies for the same model in different regions (OBS-342).
- Alert fatigue on p50 alerts (incorrect thresholds) and missing signal for routing fallback events.
- Need clearer owner responsibilities before next Dedicated capacity sales kickoff.

Audit checklist (per-dashboard):
1) Ownership: explicit owner in dashboard header and in Confluence doc (owner assigned?)
2) Primary use case: debugging, capacity ops, SRE, product health? (one-line)
3) Key KPIs present (yes/no): p50/p90/p99 latency, success rate, throughput (req/s), avg tokens per req, cost-per-1k-tokens
4) Signal quality: are metrics derived from single source-of-truth (runtime telemetry vs app logs)?
5) Cardinality hygiene: are dimensions atomized (tenant_id, model_variant, route) or are we slicing at too-high cardinality?
6) Alert mapping: each alert maps to a runbook and SLO, do we have documented thresholds?
7) Noise assessment: recent alert count (7d) and whether alerts were actionable (yes/no)
8) Visual clarity: single-page story, clear legends, time-window presets, missing annotations marked
9) Trace links: top error/latency widgets link to trace explorer filtered by trace_id or correlation_id
10) Cost visibility: when relevant, is cost broken down by model and tenant?

Scoring rubric (quick):
- 1 (fail), 2 (poor), 3 (ok), 4 (good), 5 (shipped/owned)
- Prioritize remediation by: (Impact * Confidence) / Effort.
- Example priority buckets: P0 (downtime or missing SLO), P1 (high alert noise, instrumentation gap), P2 (visual cleanup, doc updates).

Metric definitions (candidate canonical set) - short forms for engineers and dashboard templates:
- request.latency.ms.p50/p90/p99: end-to-end request latency measured at gateway (includes queuing and model time). Source: api-gateway metrics.
- serving.inference.core_latency_ms.p50/p99: time inside serving runtime from request dispatch to token stream completion, excludes gateway and network. Source: runtime-exporter.
- serving.inference.queue_ms.avg: time requests spend in runtime queues before compute. Important for autoscaling triggers.
- batching.efficiency.rate: tokens_processed / (GPU_steps * max_tokens_per_step). Lower means wasted throughput.
- kvcache.hit_rate: ratio of KV cache lookups satisfied from memory. Key signal for prefix-caching effectiveness.
- model.fallback.rate: fraction of requests sent to fallback model variant due to capacity or quality rules.
- route.error_rate: percentage of requests that returned a non-2xx or modeled failure.
- cost.per_1k_tokens_usd: rolling cost normalized by token volume; needs mapping to infra billing.

Tracing notes (practical patterns):
- Correlation id: generate at API gateway (x-redwood-cid) and propagate through all services and to model host; include in logs and traces.
- Sampling strategy: stratified sampling: always sample errors and p99 latency traces; sample a small percentage of p50s (0.5%), and higher sample rates for high-cardinality tenants for one-week windows during audits.
- Span design: treat model-host as a blackbox span with sub-spans when we have kernel-level timing (token-emit, kv-cache-lookup). Keep span count low for high-throughput flows; high-cardinality tags should be kept off spans (use attributes in logs instead).
- Trace size guardrails: limit span depth to avoid oversized traces; truncate large request payloads from trace payloads, but store a short request fingerprint.

Dashboard prioritization examples (three examples):
- Global Inference Overview dashboard: score 3 -> issues: missing KV cache metric, p99 derived from mixed sources, no runbook for model.fallback.rate. Recommended: add kvcache metric, align p99 to runtime metric, add links to runbook. Owner: Priya K. Target P1.
- Model-route troubleshooting page (per-tenant): score 2 -> issues: extreme cardinality, slow queries in dashboard backend, alerts firing for low-volume tenants. Recommended: rollup low-volume tenants into "others" by default, create drilldowns. Owner: Diego A. Target P1.
- Canary rollout dashboard: score 4 -> good latency/err visibility but missing cost per-variant. Recommended: add cost widget. Owner: Samir P. Target P2.

Remediation patterns (starter playbook):
- Align p99 definition: choose single source (prefer runtime core_latency for p99), update dashboards and alert thresholds, annotate change with date.
- Reduce cardinality: add safe rollup at dashboard layer + pre-aggregated materialized metrics for high-cardinality labels.
- Alert tuning: switch from static thresholds to adaptive windows (baseline + delta) for noisy routes.
- Tracing: add correlation id propagation library to SDKs; instrument error paths to always capture traces.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How aggressive should we be with pre-aggregation vs ad-hoc exploration? Pre-agg saves cost but reduces flexibility.
- Cost visibility: mapping infra billing to model/tenant is fuzzy for multi-tenant Dedicated pools. Need a short-term approximation strategy.
- Sampling SLA: what is the storage and cost budget for increased trace retention for audits?

Immediate next steps (owners + dates):
- Run first-pass audit of the 8 top-priority dashboards (see Confluence list) using checklist above (owner: Maya C) by 2024-11-09.
- Create PRD for p99 alignment across dashboards (owner: Priya K) by 2024-11-16.
- Implement correlation-id library and a runtime-level environment variable to enable high-trace sampling for debug builds (owner: Samir P) by 2024-12-01.

Notes to self / meeting prompts:
- Bring examples of noisy alerts (last 14 days) to sync with SRE.
- Ask platform-engineering about plans for pre-aggregation windows next quarter.

Appendix: quick search tokens to find related artifacts in Drive/GitHub/Jira:
- \"inference-dashboard\" \"kvcache\" \"core_latency\" \"model-fallback\"

Document history:
- 2024-08-15 initial draft
- 2024-09-12 added metric definitions after sync with runtime team
- 2024-11-02 updated with first-pass dashboard scoring and next steps

---
End of notes.
